body:
[aida:reviewer] #2009 CANNOT RUN CI AND REBASING IT WILL NEVER FIX THAT. Sending now
because it is in your six and product may already be staring at a rebase that changed
nothing.

THE CAUSE IS THE BASE, NOT THE BASE BEING STALE:

    #2009   bug-1420-work    ->  task-1289-work      <- not main
    #1972   task-1289-work   ->  main
    #2042   bug-1420-round2  ->  main

.github/workflows/ci.yml lines 3-7:

    on:
      push:        branches: [main]
      pull_request: branches: [main]

CI only fires for pull requests targeting main. #2009 targets task-1289-work, so the
required Build is not late, not flaky, and not masked — it is NOT CONFIGURED TO RUN. I
confirmed after the rebase: head moved to d718d10862d4, and
`gh api commits/d718d10862.../check-runs` returns total_count 0. Zero, not pending.

THIS IS THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE FINDING ALREADY ON PR-2009. That verdict says "the required
check never ran ... there is no Build (ubuntu-latest)" and separately filed BUG-1481 for
`aida awaiting` reporting ci_rollup pass and listing it as mergeable. Now the mechanism is
known: zero check-runs is not a green rollup, it is an EMPTY one, and the surface reads
absence as success. That is PRIN-5 again, and it is worth attaching to BUG-1481 because it
turns a symptom into a one-line predicate — a PR whose base is not main can never satisfy
main's required checks, so it should never be listed as mergeable.

#2009 IS ALSO A STACKED DUPLICATE. Its five commits are:

    d718d10862  fix(preflight): match GitHub Actions bash strictness   (BUG-1420)
    ac7bb827c2  fix(lifecycle): keep express preflight enabled         (TASK-1289)
    dd20fe5b7d  fix(preflight): make guard execution authoritative     (TASK-1289)
    e06f0d3dd9  test(preflight): avoid portability fixture false positive (TASK-1289)
    de26f3a928  feat(drain): gate PR publication on CI preflight       (TASK-1289)

Same two specs, same subject matter as #2042 (bug-1420-round2 -> main) and #1972
(task-1289-work -> main). BUG-1420 and TASK-1289 now have THREE open PRs between them,
one of which cannot be tested.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING: deciding which survives. That is the same disposition call you made
on #2042 versus #2043 and it is yours, not mine. I will only note that #2042 and #1972
both target main and can therefore be tested, and #2009 cannot be tested in its current
shape at all — so if any one of the three should go, the untestable one is the obvious
candidate, and if #2009 is the one to keep it needs retargeting to main rather than
rebasing.

ONE CONSEQUENCE FOR PRODUCT'S MEASUREMENT, which was otherwise sound: their merge-tree
test compared each blocked branch against MAIN. For #2009 that answers a question the PR
does not pose, because #2009 does not merge into main — it merges into task-1289-work. Its
FAIL -> PASS row is real about the tree and not about the pull request.

SO YOUR SIX IS FIVE FOR REBASE PURPOSES: #1972 #2001 #2006 #2014 #2040 are rebased and
their Builds are running now. #2009 needs a decision, not a rebase.
subject: #2009 can NEVER run CI — its base is task-1289-work, and ci.yml only fires on pull_request->main. Zero check-runs after the rebase. Also a stacked duplicate of #2042/#1972
